content:
Julian Moore: need quick alignment on telemetry schema for the batching tier selection reason codes. question is: do we emit as metric tags (labels) vs a structured event in traces/logs (or both)?

Lena Fischer: my gut says tags are going to explode cardinality if we do it wrong. but we do want dashboards like “% traffic using tier default vs override vs overload mode”

Logan Wright: +1. if we add `reason_code=<freeform>` to request metrics we’ll pay for it. if it’s a small enum we *might* be ok, but we need to be strict.

Caleb Johnson: from tracing side: easiest is add span attrs on the scheduler decision span. e.g. `batching.tier_effective`, `batching.profile_source`, `batching.reason_code`. then we can sample traces and still answer “why”.

Allison Grant: for SRE dashboards/alerts, I need a time series we can break down by reason bucket. doesn’t have to be per-request detail, but we need aggregate counts + ability to slice by tier/model/region.

Marcus Reed: current implementation draft has a bunch of decision points (tier default, model constraint, overload backpressure, dedicated override). are we thinking one reason code or multiple?

Sofia Ivanova: one. if we do multiple, it’s going to turn into JSON-in-a-label and we’ll regret it. we can have a primary reason and then a couple booleans for modifiers.

Julian Moore: ok so proposal:
- define enum `profile_source`: {"tier_default", "route_policy", "customer_override", "model_constraint", "overload_mode", "legacy_manual"}
- define enum `reason_code`: small set, stable, not user-provided
- emit in traces (structured)
- optionally emit to metrics as low-card label `profile_source` only (not full `reason_code`)

Logan Wright: i like that split. metrics labels should be <= ~10 values and only on a subset of metrics. tracing can carry the richer `reason_code`.

Allison Grant: but i still need to know overload mode % over time without querying traces.

Julian Moore: overload can be its own label/flag: `overload=1/0` or `mode={normal,overload}`. that should be stable.

Caleb Johnson: +1. and for trace shape:
- root request span already exists
- add child span `scheduler.profile_selection`
- attach attrs on that span
- also add one structured event (otel event) `batching.profile_selected` with the same attrs so we can query without relying on span names.

Lena Fischer: do we really need both span attrs + event? feels redundant.

Caleb Johnson: span attrs are fine, but events are nicer if we later add multiple decision steps. but agree we can start with attrs only.

Paula Mendes: for automated canary/rollback: we want a stable numeric counter we can gate on. e.g. “% of requests in fast tier falling back due to model constraint” should be observable without trace sampling.

Logan Wright: careful. “model constraint” as label on every request metric is probably ok (boolean-ish), but “why did model constraint happen” (unsupported kv cache, quant mismatch, max_batch_tokens cap) is where it gets large.

Ethan Park: also note Dedicated override precedence: we should be able to see whether the effective profile came from tenant override vs route policy. support will ask.

Sofia Ivanova: so maybe metrics labels:
- `tier_effective` (fast/standard/cost_efficient)
- `profile_source` (tier_default/route_policy/customer_override)
- `constraint_applied` (0/1)
- `overload_mode` (0/1)
Anything beyond that goes to tracing only.

Allison Grant: that works. I can build panels off those. for deep dives we can pivot into traces.

Marcus Reed: what about `profile_id`? super useful to debug. but it’ll cardinality explode if it’s on metrics.

Logan Wright: do NOT put `profile_id` on metrics. trace attr is ok. if you want it in logs, make it structured field.

Julian Moore: ack. so:
- `profile_id` only in traces (and maybe debug logs behind sampling)
- metrics get tier/source/flags only

Lena Fischer: naming? can we keep it consistent across runtime + console? i’ve been using “selection_reason” in code.

Sofia Ivanova: prefer `profile_source` for the high-level, `reason_code` for the detailed trace-only enum. “selection_reason” is ambiguous.

Caleb Johnson: tracing attr naming convention: `batching.profile.source`, `batching.profile.reason_code`, `batching.profile.id`, `batching.tier.effective`.

Logan Wright: +1 and please keep them flat-ish. also: no user strings, no route names, no tenant ids. those already exist elsewhere and we don’t want them copied into this span.

Paula Mendes: can we get a doc snippet with the canonical enums + “don’t add new values without review”? we’ve had issues where teams add reason strings ad hoc.

Julian Moore: yep i’ll add to the design doc + code will enforce enum (no freeform). new values require PR approval from telemetry reviewers.

Allison Grant: also please add a “unknown”/“other” bucket for forward compat. but guard that it doesn’t become default due to bugs.

Marcus Reed: for backwards compat w/ old manual batching configs, do we emit `profile_source=legacy_manual`?

Sofia Ivanova: yes, at least until we finish migration. that will help us measure adoption.

Benji Okafor: rollout angle: feature flag should allow turning off reason_code emission if telemetry costs spike. but i think with this low-card approach we’re fine.

Logan Wright: still want a kill switch for safety. also set sampling for any debug logs tied to `reason_code`.

Julian Moore: decision summary:
1) Use low-card metric labels: `tier_effective`, `profile_source`, `constraint_applied`, `overload_mode`.
2) Put detailed `reason_code` + `profile_id` in tracing only (span attrs on `scheduler.profile_selection`).
3) Enums only, no freeform strings; new enum values require telemetry review.

Lena Fischer: :thumbsup: works for me.

Allison Grant: :+1: please loop me on the enum list before merge.

Caleb Johnson: i’ll add the span + attribute keys in the tracing lib and ping Julian.

Logan Wright: thanks. when you add metrics labels, coordinate w/ me so we can sanity-check expected cardinality (tier x model x region x source x flags).

Julian Moore: will do. I’ll post the enum list here once i’ve cleaned it up.
